input: cells is an Array of exactly eight integer bits in {0,1}; n is an integer in [0,1000000000]. n=0 is an explicit extension. Integer inputs are primitive safe-integer Numbers, excluding negative zero, NaN, infinities, fractions and BigInt. Arrays are dense ordinary Arrays without holes, subclasses, proxies or accessors; strings are primitive. No concurrent mutation or modified standard built-ins are allowed. Preconditions are not dynamically validated. Size bounds do not guarantee available memory or completion within an unqualified runtime budget.
return: A fresh eight-element state after exactly n simultaneous daily updates. An interior cell becomes 1 exactly when its two prior-day neighbors agree; endpoints become 0 on each update. For n=0 return an equal fresh copy of cells.
mutation_aliasing: Neither the original eight cells nor any caller container is changed. Each daily update allocates a new eight-element state. The returned container never aliases the input; saved cycle keys contain immutable bit values, not mutable state references. The Solution instance retains no state; separate calls share no mutable result state.
numeric: There are at most 256 possible eight-bit states. At a repeated state, day-seen[key] is a strictly positive period, so the remainder divisor is never zero. n-day is nonnegative and at most 1000000000; all days, periods and remainders are exact safe integers. Booleans are explicitly converted to integer 0/1 in daily output.
complexity: At most 256 distinct states are visited before a repeat, followed by fewer than 256 residual transitions. Thus O(8*(min(n,512)+1)) work and O(8*256) retained state-key storage are conservative fixed-width bounds, assuming ordinary map costs. Daily state allocation totals at most 512 eight-element containers; only a constant number of state containers are live. Python tuple and JavaScript eight-character string key creation/hashing are charged. Map/set costs assume ordinary average O(1) operations after charging key construction/hash/comparison; no universal ECMAScript constant-time or adversarial collision-resistance guarantee is claimed.
